source.title: A Walk with SGD
source.authors: Chen Xing; Devansh Arpit; Christos Tsirigotis; Yoshua Bengio

record.tranche_reason: The study experimentally relates optimization conditions and measured loss-landscape properties to validation performance, using measures that differ from the claim versions. It does not directly test any listed version.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on SGD dynamics and validation performance. It does not test random-label memorization, width sweeps, convolutional versus fully connected networks, adaptive optimizers, fixed-epoch batch-size generalization gaps, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples. Cited findings are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own results on SGD trajectories, artificial isotropic noise, and learning-rate schedules, but none measures a listed version. Batch-size experiments measure optimization dynamics rather than held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets (V5). Hessian spectral norm versus validation accuracy is not magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness versus generalization gap (V7).
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete. The authors infer that SGD moves between valley walls above a floor containing barriers, with learning rate controlling height and mini-batch stochasticity facilitating exploration. They argue that noise structure matters: artificial isotropic noise added to full-batch gradients worsens convergence and validation performance. Their Hessian–validation association is qualitative, and they caution that conclusions may depend on architecture, dataset, and parameterization.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies loss interpolation and optimization dynamics along training trajectories, not the interventions or generalization measures in the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Learning rate affects the measured height above the valley floor; batch size affects the cosine between consecutive gradients and parameter distance from initialization. The authors report that these roles differ across their tested settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Artificial isotropic noise added to full-batch gradients worsens convergence and validation performance relative to noiseless GD for VGG-11 and ResNet-56 on CIFAR-10 and an MLP on MNIST.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adding artificial isotropic gradient noise to full-batch GD can worsen training convergence and validation performance in these settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Hessian spectral norm generally decreases during training and increases toward its end, alongside an eventual validation-accuracy drop in VGG-11 and ResNet-56. The authors describe the association as mild or rough.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unscaled Hessian spectral norm and validation accuracy can be inversely associated along individual training trajectories.

fits_no_version.finding: Smaller batches produce less negative consecutive-gradient cosine and greater exploration, whereas learning rate mainly controls height above the interpolated valley floor.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch size and learning rate have qualitatively different effects on SGD trajectory geometry in the tested settings.

fits_no_version.finding: At batch size 100, tuned trapezoid learning-rate schedules achieve similar or better performance than cyclical schedules; schedules increasing learning rate during training are described as slightly better.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Repeated learning-rate cycles are unnecessary for comparable performance in the tested VGG-11 and ResNet-56 CIFAR-10 experiments.

record.problems: The paper describes its experiments as qualitative. The isotropic-noise validation comparisons are figure-based and lack numerical values and reported uncertainty. The Hessian/validation relationship is described as mild or rough correlation and is not a direct test of a generalization gap.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out. The Hessian spectral-norm and validation-accuracy trajectory is mentioned under fits_no_version, but is not mapped to V7 because it is not magnitude-aware sharpness and does not compare networks at similarly low training loss.

untested.parts: No own comparison of random-label memorization with natural-label and random-label held-out accuracy.
No width sweep or test-error comparison beyond the width needed to fit.
No controlled comparison of convolutional and fully connected classifiers, learned locality, or convolution-derived initialization.
No adaptive-optimizer versus SGD held-out comparison under limited or broader tuning.

No held-out performance comparison across batch sizes with epochs held fixed, or test of recipes recovering a large-batch penalty. Batch-size comparisons concern gradient angles and exploration; isotropic-noise comparisons train until loss saturation.
No dropout intervention or comparison involving training-set size, augmentation, or removal of dropout and weight decay.
No magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation measure, ranking of generalization gaps among similarly fitted networks, or comparison against norm- and margin-based measures.
No removal of examples selected by memorization influence, retraining, or random-removal control.

record.verdict_notes: No listed-version verdict is warranted. States marked cannot_determine refer to applicability to the claim versions, not uncertainty about the explicitly reported isotropic-noise deterioration. The supplied text contains figure captions rather than readable numerical plot values.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fit and held-out performance on natural versus random labels.
Test error as width increases past the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier generalization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under the stated tuning conditions.
Held-out performance across batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout effects on held-out error and its interaction with dataset size or other regularization.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness compared with other generalization measures.
Effect of removing memorized training examples on test accuracy.

rows.subject: VGG-11
rows.operation_detail: Trained with full-batch gradient descent without added noise; compared with GD using artificial isotropic gradient noise.
rows.note: The text says the isotropic-noise models have worse validation performance than the noiseless GD model, but gives no numerical values for this comparison.
rows.check: The noiseless-GD comparator does not measure any listed version; numerical validation accuracy is unavailable in the supplied text.

rows.subject: VGG-11
rows.stage_stated: trained using GD with artificial isotropic noise
rows.operation_detail: Added isotropic Gaussian noise to the full-dataset gradient, with variance set using the maximum gradient variance at initialization multiplied by 0.1 or 0.05.
rows.baseline: GD without noise; numerical validation accuracy not stated
rows.value: figure only; text says convergence and generalization are worse than with GD
rows.note: The paper reports a qualitative deterioration versus noiseless GD; it also says the isotropic-noise models get stuck in training loss.
rows.check: The reported deterioration with artificial isotropic noise is explicit, but does not measure any listed version, so partial is inappropriate. The row also combines two noise conditions and training loss with validation accuracy.
